# Corpus samples

One representative document per class, so the corpus is concrete rather than
described. The rationale for holding two classes, and the simplifications that
choice implies, are in
[RESEARCH_DESIGN.md](RESEARCH_DESIGN.md#corpus-construction) — this file is only
the material itself.

Retrieval draws `BASELINE_N_NOTEBOOKS` solution artifacts and `METADATA_K`
scoping artifacts per run, identically in every condition.

---

## Class 1 — Solution artifacts (`notebook_summaries`)

**What it is.** One abstract per Code4ML notebook, generated by a pinned Haiku
against `SUMMARY_SYSTEM` (`ingest/ingest_summaries.py`) over the notebook's
concatenated code cells, capped at 60k characters. The notebook, not the cell, is
the retrieval unit. Production analogue: internal analyses, prior model work,
postmortems.

**Sample** — `nb_1469586`, from `new-york-city-taxi-fare-prediction`, 307 words:

> This notebook addresses taxi fare prediction on New York City data by building a
> deep neural network after heavy preprocessing and feature engineering.
>
> The author works with a large training set (over one million rows), loading it in
> chunks of 2^20 rows to manage memory constraints. The target is fare_amount in
> dollars, bounded between $2 and $150 after outlier removal. Key preprocessing
> steps include computing haversine distance in miles between pickup and dropoff
> coordinates, extracting temporal features (year, month, day of week, time of day
> encoded as 0-2399), and binning all spatial and temporal features into discrete
> intervals. The spatial binning is particularly granular: latitude and longitude
> each receive 700 bins across the New York bounding box, distance gets 400 bins,
> and time of day gets 480 bins. After cleaning and reducing the dataset by 25
> percent (retaining ~750k rows), the author normalizes features to [0,1] using
> training set min-max values, which are saved and applied identically to the test
> set.
>
> The model is a sequential dense network with four hidden layers of 32, 32, 32,
> and 128 units respectively, all using softmax activation (an unusual choice for
> regression). Dropout at 0.5 and batch normalization follow each hidden layer. The
> output layer uses relu activation with MSE loss. Training uses the Nadam
> optimizer, 10 epochs, and batch size 512, with validation split of approximately
> 0.1 percent (about 7.5k examples). The notebook monitors training via mean
> squared error and mean absolute error on both training and validation sets.
>
> The approach demonstrates practical techniques for handling massive tabular
> datasets: chunked loading, aggressive binning for dimensionality control, and
> memory-conscious dtype selection (float16 for normalized lower-range features,
> float32 for coordinates). The validation scheme holds out a small fixed portion
> rather than cross-validation, and predictions are rounded to two decimal places
> before submission, reflecting the dollar currency format of the target variable.

**What to notice.** Problem framing opens the summary; concrete specifics survive
(700 bins, Nadam, batch 512, float16); the validation scheme and its limits are
named; and the appraisal is critical rather than admiring — *"softmax activation
(an unusual choice for regression)"*, and the observation that a 0.1% validation
split is not cross-validation. That last property matters: the corpus is meant to
be weighed, not adopted, and a corpus of uncritical praise would not support
that.

Every document in this class is one model under one prompt, so they share a
register that a real knowledge base would not. That homogeneity is recorded as a
structural limitation in
[RESEARCH_DESIGN.md](RESEARCH_DESIGN.md#threats-to-validity).

---

## Class 2 — Problem-scoping artifacts (`competition_metadata`)

**What it is.** Problem statements as posed, before anyone has solved them. No
LLM step — raw text, chunked at 4,096 characters and embedded directly.
Production analogue: project briefs, scoping docs, model-card intended-use
sections, ML intake tickets.

Two sources feed it.

### 2a — Code4ML `competitions.csv` descriptions (936 competitions)

> Planning a celebration is a balancing act of preparing just enough food to go
> around without being stuck eating the same leftovers for the next week. The key
> is anticipating how many guests will come. Grupo Bimbo must weigh similar
> considerations as it strives to meet daily consumer demand for fresh bakery
> products on the shelves of over 1 million stores along its 45,000 routes across
> Mexico.
>
> Currently, daily inventory calculations are performed by direct delivery sales
> employees who must single-handedly predict the forces of supply, demand, and
> hunger based on their personal experiences with each store. With some breads
> carrying a one week shelf life, the acceptable margin for error is small.
>
> In this competition, Grupo Bimbo invites Kagglers to develop a model to
> accurately forecast inventory demand based on historical sales data. […]

Carried alongside as metadata: `task_category` (here `tabular data`) and
`evaluation_metric` (here `RMSLE`), where Code4ML supplies them.

**Honest note on this source.** These are organizer marketing copy as much as
specification — motivation-heavy, light on data schema. They also carry raw
quoting artifacts from the CSV (leading `` '` `` and trailing `` `' ``), which
are ingested as-is. Both are representative of real scoping documents, which are
rarely written as clean specifications.

### 2b — mle-bench `description.md` (the 22 Lite competitions)

Authoritative specifications for the evaluation competitions, and the same text
the pipeline receives as `raw_problem`. Longer and more structured than 2a:

> \# Overview
>
> \## Description
>
> Innovative materials design is needed to tackle some of the most important
> health, environmental, energy, social, and economic challenges of this century.
> In particular, improving the properties of materials that are intrinsically
> connected to the generation and utilization of energy is crucial if we are to
> mitigate environmental damage due to a growing global demand. [Transparent
> conductors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transparent_conducting_film) are an
> important class of compounds that are both electrically conductive and have a
> low absorption in the visible range, which are typically competing properties.
> […]

Leave-one-out means a competition never retrieves its own description: when
specifying competition X, only the other competitions' scoping documents are
reachable.

---

## Provenance of these samples

The solution artifact is drawn from `results/summary_prompt_validation.json`,
generated by the current `SUMMARY_SYSTEM` and pinned `SUMMARY_MODEL`. The
scoping artifacts are read from `data/raw/`, which is what `ingest_metadata`
chunks and embeds without modification. Refresh these if the summary prompt
changes again.
